court: Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit

issues.label: Scope of appellate jurisdiction under 1252
issues.why: Court must confirm jurisdiction over the final order and any limits on reviewing factual versus legal determinations.

issues.label: Standard of review for factual findings
issues.why: Nexus and acquiescence findings are reviewed for substantial evidence, framing what the court can disturb.

issues.label: Exhaustion of PSG claims before IJ
issues.why: BIA declined to reach 'Salvadoran woman' and 'family members of witnesses to crime' as unexhausted, raising whether they were properly preserved.

issues.label: Which agency decision to review
issues.why: BIA adopted and affirmed the IJ, so the court must determine which reasoning is under review.

issues.label: Political opinion as protected ground
issues.why: Court must decide whether opposing violence/favoring rule of law is a cognizable political opinion and whether applicant holds it.

issues.label: Imputed political opinion
issues.why: Even without personally holding the opinion, persecutor's imputation of one could establish a protected ground.

issues.label: Nexus for political opinion claim
issues.why: Whether Fabian's personal revenge motive precludes a political nexus must be assessed.

issues.label: Cognizability of proposed PSGs
issues.why: Each group must meet particularity, social distinction, and immutability requirements.

issues.label: Nexus for 'nuclear family of Porfiria' PSG
issues.why: Family membership is a paradigmatic PSG, so whether it was one central reason for targeting is critical.

issues.label: 'One central reason' standard for asylum nexus
issues.why: Court must apply the correct mixed-motive standard rather than requiring sole cause.

issues.label: Mixed-motive analysis with revenge/personal motives
issues.why: Personal revenge and protected-ground motives can coexist, requiring proper mixed-motive treatment.

issues.label: Gender-based nexus for female PSGs
issues.why: Whether abuse of both sexes defeats a gender nexus for 'Salvadoran women' and 'females as property.'

issues.label: Membership in 'family of prosecutorial witnesses' PSG
issues.why: Court must decide whether J.P.A.'s photo identification qualifies her as a witness making applicant a member.

issues.label: Derivative applicant J.P.A.'s status
issues.why: J.P.A.'s claim depends on principal's, but her direct witness role may raise independent considerations.

issues.label: Past persecution and burden-shifting presumption
issues.why: A past-persecution finding would shift the burden regarding future persecution.

issues.label: Well-founded fear of future persecution
issues.why: Court must assess objective and subjective components independent of past harm.

issues.label: Persecution by non-state actors
issues.why: Fabian is a private actor, requiring government unable/unwilling to protect analysis.

issues.label: Government unwillingness/inability to protect
issues.why: Police failure to interview or prosecute bears on whether the state can control the persecutor.

issues.label: Internal relocation possibility
issues.why: Whether applicant could safely relocate within El Salvador affects asylum eligibility.

issues.label: Withholding of removal standard
issues.why: The clear-probability standard differs from asylum and requires separate analysis.

issues.label: CAT acquiescence standard
issues.why: Whether official failure to prosecute amounts to acquiescence/willful blindness must be determined.

issues.label: CAT likelihood of torture
issues.why: CAT requires showing more likely than not to be tortured, independent of protected ground.

issues.label: Whether death threats constitute torture
issues.why: Court must assess if the feared harm meets CAT's severity definition of torture.

issues.label: Adverse-credibility not at issue
issues.why: IJ found applicant credible, so accepted facts must be taken as true in the analysis.

issues.label: Adequacy of BIA's single-judge reasoning
issues.why: Whether the BIA's brief affirmance adequately addressed arguments affects remand considerations.

issues.label: Failure to consider evidence claim
issues.why: Applicant argues the IJ ignored evidence, requiring review of whole-record consideration.
